card.subject: accountancy
card.front: On admission of a new partner, how are the firm’s accumulated profits distributed?
card.back: The new partner is not entitled to have any share in such accumulated profits. These are distributed among the partners by transferring it to their capital current accounts in old profit sharing ratio.
card.quote: The new partner is not entitled to have any share in such accumulated profits. These are distributed among the partners by transferring it to their capital current accounts in old profit sharing ratio.

source.section: 2.6 Adjustment for Accumulated Profits and Losses

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ____.
card.back: The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ratio of sacrifice.
card.quote: The amount of premium brought in by the new partner is shared by the existing partners in their ratio of sacrifice.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, ____ is passed in the books of the firm.
card.back: If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm.
card.quote: If this amount is paid to the old partners directly (privately) by the new partner, no entry is passed in the books of the firm.

question.body: At the admission of T, X and Y are the existing partners, sharing profits in the ratio 3:2. The agreed profit-sharing ratio after T’s admission is X:Y:T = 4:3:3. The firm has an untransferred reserve of ₹24,000, a general reserve of ₹18,000 and a credit balance of ₹33,000 in the Profit and Loss Account. All three balances are accumulated profits from before T’s admission. What amounts should be allocated to X, Y and T, respectively, from these accumulated profits?

card.subject: accountancy
card.back: The ratio in which the old partners agree to sacrifice their share of profit in favour of the incoming partner is called sacrificing ratio.
card.quote: The ratio in which the old partners agree to sacrifice their share of profit in favour of the incoming partner is called sacrificing ratio.

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill premium credited to old partners is retained in business: what additional entry is passed?
card.back: If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed.
card.quote: If the partners decide that the amount of premium for goodwill credited to their capital accounts should be retained in business, an additional entry is not passed.

source.section: 2.5.5.1 When the new Partner brings goodwill in cash

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is ____ at the time of admission of a partner.
card.back: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is written off at the time of admission of a partner.
card.quote: Goodwill, if existing in the books of the firm, it is written off at the time of admission of a partner.

source.section: When goodwill already exists in books

card.subject: accountancy
card.front: Goodwill appearing in the books will be ____ by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their ____.
card.back: Goodwill appearing in the books will be written-off by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their old profit sharing ratio.
card.quote: Goodwill appearing in the books will be written-off by debiting old partners' capital accounts in their old profit sharing ratio.

source.section: When goodwill exists in the books
